gaps.availableEvidence: core/action-authority.js accepts an action when the per-action table carries a spec for it OR the module boundary charter lists it in owns[]. The table carries 61 specs, each naming an owner, a service, an audit vocabulary and a backend requirement. The charter declares 124 capability names across 29 modules, of which 82 have no per-action spec. The charter list mixes writes with view capabilities, so its entries cannot be read as actions without checking each one.
gaps.reasonRequired: An action authorised only by the charter runs with no declared service, no declared audit vocabulary and no declared backend requirement, while an action in the table runs with all four. Nothing states which authority governs when they disagree.
gaps.impactOfAbsence: Governed writes exist that this documentation can name but cannot describe: the FastTrack escalation and owner-notification actions are authorised by the charter alone and carry no audit vocabulary of their own.
gaps.operationalRisk: A write reaches the system of record without the audit event a reader of the governance table would expect it to write.
gaps.requiredAuthoritativeSource: The platform technical owner, as the owner of both configurations.
gaps.resolutionCriteria: Every name the runtime will accept as an action has a per-action record, or the charter states explicitly which of its entries are actions and which are views.

gaps.subject: Some governed writes cannot be named from their call site
gaps.missingInformation: The action name at the call site, for the modules that pass it as a variable.
gaps.availableEvidence: 4 module(s) — activities, executive, fasttrack, user-admin — call executeOwnedAction() with the action passed as a variable. Their actions are recovered from the per-action table and, where the name also appears as a literal in the module, from the boundary charter. Every recovered step is classified Inferred and says which recovery produced it.
gaps.reasonRequired: A step recovered by reading two artifacts together is weaker evidence than one read from a single call site, and the difference should not be invisible to a reader.
gaps.impactOfAbsence: For these modules, the mapping from a control the operator presses to the action it raises is a reading rather than a fact.
gaps.operationalRisk: An action could be raised that no artifact declares, and this documentation would not show it.
gaps.requiredAuthoritativeSource: The module source, if the call sites are changed to name their actions literally.
gaps.resolutionCriteria: Each call site names its action literally, or the module declares the set of names it dispatches.

gaps.subject: Nothing fires an escalation when a service-level clock expires
gaps.missingInformation: An automatic trigger: a scheduled check, a flow, or a rule that raises the escalation when the acknowledgement or completion date passes.
gaps.availableEvidence: 6 routing rows carrying acknowledgement and completion day counts, which core/assignment-cascade.js turns into dated ack and due fields on the assignment. Breach IS detected — modules/fasttrack.js classifies every tracked item Breached, Due soon or Unassigned against its due date and reports the counts. Escalation IS available — governed actions raise an escalation level, force priority to urgent, write an escalation record, queue an owner notification, and resolve an open escalation. Every one of them requires an operator to press a control.
gaps.reasonRequired: The detection and the response both exist; only the connection between the clock and the response is missing. A clock whose expiry raises nothing is a measurement, not a control.
gaps.impactOfAbsence: A breach is visible only to someone who opens the FastTrack workspace and looks. Nothing reaches an owner who does not.
gaps.operationalRisk: Overdue matters accumulate unseen between visits to the workspace.
gaps.resolutionCriteria: A scheduled check or a flow raises the escalation and the notification when a clock expires, without waiting for an operator to open a screen.
